title: SHAM-Bench: A Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.27370v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Span-level hallucination detection pinpoints unsupported content in LLM outputs, enabling actionable feedback and targeted mitigation. Existing evaluations for span-level hallucination detection methods are fragmented across tasks, annotation formats, and metrics, and most span-level datasets cover only a single NLG domain, making it difficult to assess whether a detection method actually generalizes across tasks and domains. In this paper, we introduce SHAM-Bench (Span-level Hallucination Benchmark Across Multiple Tasks), a unified benchmark for span-level hallucination detection spanning six NLG tasks, aggregated from existing human-annotated datasets totaling 6,461 examples under a common schema and evaluation protocol. translated_title: SHAM-Bench：一个跨多任务的片段级幻觉检测基准
translated_abstract: 片段级幻觉检测能够精确定位大语言模型输出中缺乏依据支持的内容，从而提供可操作的反馈和有针对性的缓解措施。目前针对片段级幻觉检测方法的评估在任务、标注格式和指标上较为零散，且大多数片段级数据集仅覆盖单一的自然语言生成（NLG）领域，这使得难以评估某个检测方法是否真正能够在不同任务和领域之间泛化。在本文中，我们提出了SHAM-Bench（跨多任务的片段级幻觉检测基准），这是一个统一的片段级幻觉检测基准，涵盖六个NLG任务，通过统一的模式和评估协议，从现有人工标注数据集中聚合而成，共计6,461个样本。利用SHAM-Bench，我们评估了现有的幻觉检测方法，发现经过微调的检测器通常在域内表现良好，但在分布偏移下性能下降，而基于提示的推理方法（摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 提出了SHAM-Bench——一个涵盖六个NLG任务、共6461个样本的统一片段级幻觉检测基准，评估发现微调检测器在域内表现良好但在分布偏移下退化，而基于提示的推理方法泛化能力更强。
en_tdlr: We introduce SHAM-Bench, a unified span-level hallucination detection benchmark spanning six NLG tasks with 6,461 examples, showing that fine-tuned detectors perform well in-domain but degrade under distribution shift, whereas prompt-based reasoning methods generalize better.
